stories.title: Datasets for the environmental assessment of the average organic and conventional agricultural production of chickpeas and lentils in metropolitan France
stories.description: This data paper presents life cycle inventories (LCI) and life cycle impact assessments (LCIA) derived from responses to a nationwide questionnaire distributed to French chickpea and lentil producers by Terres Inovia in 2022. The average French production of lentils, chickpeas, and their respective conventional and organic variants were modelled separately, resulting in a total of four products assessed. The MEANS-InOut platform was used to generate the LCIs, using Ecoinvent 3.9 and Agribalyse 4 as background databases. The LCIA calculations were performed using the “EF 3.1 (adapted)” characterization method as well as “IMPACT World + Midpoint V1.03” and “ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint (H) V1.08 / World (2010) H” to accommodate users of any of these methods. As data on these types of crops are very scarce, the addition of this data to the literature contributes to enabling more robust environmental comparisons across crops, countries, and farming practices, and support LCA practitioners in integrating French pulses into assessments. The datasets could also inform improvement in pulse-based cropping systems and downstream products LCAs by identifying key environmental drivers.

stories.title: One-pot synthesis of carbon nanotube /graphene composite phase change materials based on Pickering emulsion for solar thermal storage
stories.description: The practical deployment of phase change materials (PCMs) is frequently constrained by two intrinsic drawbacks. respectively low thermal conductivity and susceptibility to leakage during solid–liquid phase change. To address these issues, this study reports the synthesis of composite PCMs comprising hexadecanol encapsulated within a three-dimensional carbon nanotube (CNT)/reduced graphene oxide (RGO) network, fabricated via a one-pot Pickering emulsion method using graphene oxide (GO) as the stabilizer. The resulting CNT/RGO scaffold concurrently enhances thermal transport and structural integrity. Specifically, the thermal conductivity of the composite reaches 125.40% of that of pristine hexadecanol, while the latent heat capacity is substantially retained. Furthermore, the composite exhibits an enhanced photothermal response under simulated solar irradiation. These characteristics render the developed material a promising candidate for solar thermal storage applications .

stories.title: A numerical study of oil pad morphology as an important indicator of separation efficiency in a horizontal three-phase gravity separator
stories.description: Developing unconventional oil resources requires stable surface facilities for separating highly viscous oil–water–gas mixtures. Horizontal three-phase gravity separators are widely used but their performance remains limited because separation failure is governed by residence time, bulk operating conditions, and even internal phase redistribution near the weir. Therefore, we investigate whether oil pad morphology can serve as a practical indicator of separation efficiency. Three-dimensional CFD simulations were performed for 16 operating cases by varying inlet flow rates and water outlet pressures. The phase interactions were accurately described by combining the Eulerian multiphase model with the k–ε turbulence and interfacial area concentration models. The results demonstrate that separation efficiency decreases with increasing water outlet pressure for all inlet conditions. Analyzing the morphology of the three-dimensional oil pad near the weir reveals that high-efficiency cases feature a laterally continuous oil pad, whereas low-efficiency cases exhibit sidewall thinning, creating preferential water pathways. Stable separation is successfully achieved when the height of the oil pad bottom remains below 95.4% of the weir height. Furthermore, wider pads correlate to better efficiency, and an empirical correlation based on outlet-pressure ratio and oil-pad width reproduces the CFD-derived separation efficiencies with an MAE of 2.70%.
